walkthroughs.body_html:
Priority Health Issues — a core area of A-Level Food Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Priority Health Issues brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Priority Health Issues.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why are dried foods less prone to spoilage?
options: It tells you the calorie content.
Bacteria do not like dry textures.
Drying adds preservatives.
Low water activity prevents microorganisms from growing.

mcqs.q: Why does food provenance matter to consumers?
options: It affects environmental impact, quality, ethics, and supports local economies.
Because they are illegal.
It tells you the calorie content.
Only the price matters.

mcqs.q: Why must the 14 major allergens be highlighted on UK food labels?
options: To advertise that the food contains them.
Because they are illegal.
Drying adds preservatives.
Reactions can be severe or life-threatening, so consumers must identify them at a glance.
